papers.title_en: CarlHOI: Counterfactual Predictive Imagination for Generalizable Multi-Humanoid Object Interaction under Constrained Environments
papers.authors: Wenjie Lin, Jin Wei-Kocsis
papers.evidence: 面向多人形物体交互的关系潜世界模型与强化学习控制
papers.tldr: 多个人形机器人协同搬运物体时，学到的协作策略难以适应未见的环境约束，如需要绕行或改变队形。本文提出CarlHOI，构建以反事实为锚的关系潜世界模型，通过预测想象生成反事实未来，从而在不重训底层协作控制策略的情况下完成适应。实验表明该方法能在受限环境中实现可泛化的多人形机器人物体交互。
papers.abstract_en: Recent advances in physics-based humanoid control enable teams of varying sizes to coordinate their movements and cooperatively transport shared objects. However, adapting learned cooperative behaviors to unseen environmental constraints remains challenging, particularly when obstacles require coordinated detours and changes in team configuration. We propose CarlHOI, a counterfactual predictive imagination framework built upon a counterfactual-anchored relational latent world model (CarlWM) for human-object interaction (HOI), enabling multi-humanoid teams to adapt to unseen environmental constraints without retraining their underlying cooperative control policies. CarlHOI explicitly represents the shared object, individual humanoids, and environmental obstacles as interacting entities. Trained offline using counterfactual simulator rollouts, the model imagines alternative collective futures under different shared waypoint commands, predicting how the coupled humanoid team and object would respond. By evaluating these imagined outcomes through predicted progress, failure, and contact risks, and long-horizon value estimates, CarlHOI selects adaptive guidance commands while preserving the pretrained cooperative controller. We introduce a benchmark comprising three challenging obstacle-constrained transport tasks to evaluate adaptation and generalization. Despite being trained exclusively with four humanoids, our model generalizes without retraining to teams of two to ten humanoids, unseen obstacle geometries and placements, unseen objects, and novel combinations of environmental constraints. Extensive experiments demonstrate improved cooperative transport success over evaluated baselines across diverse configurations. Results highlight the potential of counterfactual predictive imagination to extend pretrained multi-humanoid cooperative skills beyond their original training conditions.

papers.title_en: ReGATE: Recurrent Gated Visual Fusion for Reactive Humanoid-Object Interaction
papers.authors: Hao Zhu, Jorge Pe\~na-Queralta
papers.evidence: 面向物体抓取、搬运与释放的人形全身控制
papers.tldr: 针对人形机器人在视觉不完整条件下完成物体抓取、搬运与释放的全身控制难题，本文提出ReGATE控制器，融合第一视角深度、本体感知与在线运动接触指令，并借助教师-学生框架中的循环门控适配器在线估计物体几何与物理接触，无需外部位姿估计器。课程化训练与相位感知初始化提升了短暂接触过渡的覆盖度，使反应式人形物体交互更加鲁棒。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinating object acquisition, transport, and release from onboard sensing while responding to user commands and incomplete visual observations. We present ReGATE, a whole-body controller that combines egocentric depth, proprioception, and online locomotion and contact commands. Built on a teacher-student framework, ReGATE integrates interaction-state estimation through a recurrent adapter that predicts object geometry and physical contact without an external object-pose estimator. Head-wise and global gates regulate visual updates to a proprioceptive pathway. A visual-grounding and corruption curriculum trains the adapter, while phase-aware initialization increases coverage of brief contact transitions. In simulation, ReGATE achieves 85.2% success across 330 static-object acquisition trials, compared with 48.5% for VisualMimic under the same protocol, and 85.9% across 440 moving-object acquisition trials. Deployment on a Unitree G1 demonstrates commanded grasp-transport-release sequences and acquisition of laterally displaced boxes. A qualitative hardware experiment further demonstrates successful box acquisition when the camera is occluded after an initial observation and before the contact command. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to extend recurrent gated fusion of onboard depth and proprioception from perceptive locomotion to humanoid loco-manipulation under interrupted visual sensing.

papers.title_en: HLO-AMP: Hierarchical Loco-Manipulation from Object-Aware Motion Priors
papers.authors: Jean-Pierre Sleiman, Bilal Hammoud, He Li, Jonathan Foster, Sylvain Bertrand, Jessica K. Hodgins, Farbod Farshidian
papers.evidence: 人形全身移动操作与物体感知运动先验
papers.tldr: 现有人形移动操作分层流程中，底层全身控制器训练时未纳入被操作物体，仅用随机末端力扰动近似负载，难以复现真实的多接触力旋量。本文提出HLO-AMP，将底层控制器训练为物体感知的运动先验，通过重定向动作数据的运动模仿得到单一策略。结果表明该方法在接近负载极限时仍能保持稳定的全身移动操作，动作也更自然。
papers.abstract_en: Hierarchical pipelines for humanoid loco-manipulation typically pair a task-agnostic whole-body controller (WBC) with a downstream task policy. Such WBCs are often trained through manual reward shaping, which yields visibly machine-like motions; more consequentially, they are trained without the manipulated object in the scene. Object dynamics are instead approximated through randomized end-effector force disturbances, a proxy that fails to reproduce the distributed multi-contact wrench a real payload applies across the arms and torso, with the gap becoming critical near the platform's payload limit. In this work, we train the low-level (LL) controller itself as an object-aware motion prior: a single policy trained via motion imitation on retargeted motion-capture (MoCap) references that span the core motion primitives of the downstream task, with the manipulated object physically present in the scene. This single stage inherits natural human-like coordination from the references and absorbs the realistic contact wrench at its source, while exposing the same compact task-space command interface used by command-tracking WBCs. A reference-free high-level (HL) policy is then trained on top, with its action channel anchored to the empirical envelope of the low-level training data so that it generalizes the priors to a long-horizon multi-stage task while structurally preventing queries that would push the low level off-distribution. We instantiate the framework on a Unitree G1 for bimanual box pick-and-place: the same deployed policy generalizes across object masses and dimensions, initial and goal poses, and reactively recovers from intentional drops mid-carry. Video: https://youtu.be/viR_ULnRDQQ.

papers.title_en: H^2MARL: Hierarchical Heterogeneous Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning for Humanoid Robot Control
papers.authors: Xuemin Hu, Kaixin Li, Qingqing Xia, Yuxin Wang, Wei Xie, Bo Tang, Long Chen
papers.evidence: 面向人形全身控制的分层异构多智能体强化学习
papers.tldr: 人形机器人全身控制面临高维耦合动力学与关节自由度物理异质性的挑战，现有方法要么粗粒度划分智能体，要么直接套用通用算法，导致动作不协调。本文提出H^2MARL分层异构多智能体强化学习框架，基于关节自由度级物理异质性进行策略分解。方法协调高层规划与低层执行以产生一致运动。该工作为人形机器人全身控制提供了有效的强化学习方案。
papers.abstract_en: Coordinated whole-body control of humanoid robots remains challenging due to high-dimensional coupled dynamics and substantial physical heterogeneity across joint degrees of freedom (JDoFs). Existing multi-agent reinforcement learning methods either employ coarse agent partitions or directly apply generic heterogeneous-agent algorithms, while hierarchical controllers commonly optimize high-level planning and low-level execution independently, leading to uncoordinated motion. In this paper, we propose H^2MARL, a hierarchical heterogeneous multi-agent reinforcement learning framework with two key mechanisms. We first formulate humanoid whole-body control using a JDoF-level physical-heterogeneity-aware policy factorization, where each torque-actuated JDoF is conditioned on an explicit descriptor of its actuation, kinematic, and dynamic properties. Moreover, we develop a closed-loop policy-executor co-optimization mechanism that jointly adapts the high-level pose planner and the low-level joint executor using shared interaction trajectories, thereby reducing the distribution mismatch between planning and execution. Extensive experiments in MuJoCo and Isaac Gym demonstrate that H^2MARL consistently improves locomotion stability, gait coordination, and motion quality over homogeneous, coarse-grained, and independently optimized alternatives.

papers.title_en: SUGARv2: Learning Diverse Visual Humanoid Loco-Manipulation Skills from Synthesized Interaction References
papers.authors: Tianshu Wu, Tianxiang Gui, Yue Chen, Tingxu Liu, Ziye Peng, Guangjie Yang, Xiangqi Kong, Ye Shi, Jingya Wang, Hao Dong
papers.evidence: 通过参考模仿学习视觉人形移动操作技能
papers.tldr: 扩展视觉人形移动操作技能需要大量示范采集与逐任务奖励设计，人力成本很高。SUGARv2提出统一框架，复用任务模板在不同空间配置下合成协调的机器人与物体交互参考，并以参考驱动的模仿学习作为跨任务共享目标。该流程降低了任务特定奖励设计与训练开销，可习得多样化的视觉人形移动操作技能。
papers.abstract_en: Scaling up visual humanoid loco-manipulation skill acquisition requires reducing the human effort needed as tasks and spatial configurations expand, particularly in demonstration collection and task-specific training design. We present SUGARv2, a unified framework for learning diverse visual humanoid loco-manipulation skills through interaction reference synthesis and a shared training pipeline. To obtain diverse references at low cost, we adapt reusable task templates to different spatial configurations, synthesizing coordinated robot and object motions. To reduce task-specific reward design and training effort, we use reference-based imitation as a common learning objective across tasks. We first train privileged teachers to execute these references, then train visual policies through teacher distillation and reinforcement learning with the same reference-based mimic rewards, using diverse object instances and visual domain randomization to support visual generalization and sim-to-real transfer. Across five humanoid loco-manipulation tasks, SUGARv2 achieves a mean success rate of 91.0% in simulation. Deployment on a real humanoid robot further demonstrates successful sim-to-real transfer for whole-body manipulation. These results demonstrate the framework's potential for learning diverse visual humanoid loco-manipulation skills.

papers.title_en: Kimodo-Policy: Learning Kinematic Action Models for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.authors: Yunheng Wang, Jiaxi Zhang, Wei Lu, Yuetong Fang, Taowen Wang, Yixiao Feng, Shuning Zhang, Junzhe Xu, Yichi Wang, Zizhao Yuan, Kailun Huang, Lusong Li, Mingqian Zhou, Zecui Zeng, Renjing Xu
papers.evidence: 基于运动学动作模型的人形机器人全身移动操作
papers.tldr: 人形机器人移动操作需要持续协调高维全身运动，而视觉-语言-动作模型与世界动作模型迁移的语义和视觉动力学先验未必刻画机器人自身的运动结构。作者提出运动学动作模型KAM，将全身运动作为直接预训练目标，以预训练运动生成器作为动作生成主干，并通过任务条件、视觉观测与执行反馈对齐时序与跨身体协调先验。Kimodo-Policy作为首个实例验证了该范式在人形移动操作上的有效性。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires continuous coordination of high-dimensional whole-body motion to realize task objectives. While vision-language-action models and world action models transfer semantic and visual-dynamics priors to robot control, these priors do not necessarily capture the structure of robot motion. We introduce Kinematic Action Models (KAMs), a paradigm that treats whole-body motion as a direct pretraining target and uses a pretrained motion generator as the primary action-generation backbone. KAMs ground learned temporal and cross-body coordination priors through task conditioning, visual observations, and execution feedback. We present Kimodo-Policy as an initial instantiation, combining a frozen Kimodo text-to-motion backbone with lightweight ControlNet-based visual conditioning. A root-body-hand hierarchy coordinates locomotion and manipulation, while motion-history conditioning and repeated action-chunk prediction bridge motion synthesis and closed-loop control. Following large-scale loco-manipulation pretraining, the policy achieves the highest overall success among compared policies on multi-task HumanoidArena (72.14%), competitive performance on SIMPLE, and 60% mean success across eight real-world tasks, with 678M parameters (92M trainable). Ablations support the contribution of the pretrained motion backbone. Together, these results provide initial evidence for motion generation as a complementary foundation for humanoid action learning.

papers.title_en: $\Sigma$-LeWM: Learning World Models via S-Information for Robot Control
papers.authors: Xinrui Zu, Michael Przystupa, Zhao Yang, Shujian Yu, Kevin Sebastian Luck
papers.evidence: 带额外潜在动力学损失的联合嵌入预测架构世界模型用于机器人控制
papers.tldr: 世界模型已成为机器人的基于模型控制方法，但早期架构依赖解码器防止模式塌缩，近期如联合嵌入预测架构转而只用潜在前向动力学与熵正则项学习嵌入。本文在LeWorldModel基础上额外引入反向动力学预测器与逆动力学动作预测器两个潜在损失，对嵌入施加更强的结构约束。实验表明该结构使潜在表示更可预测，在操作与运动控制任务上取得更好效果。
papers.abstract_en: World models have increasingly been applied as a model-based control method for robotics tasks such as manipulation and locomotion. While early world model architectures relied on decoders to prevent mode collapse and learn a predictable latent space, recent works on world models, such as Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture or LeWorldModel, increasingly aim to learn embeddings without a grounding decoder, utilising only a latent forward dynamics predictor and a stabilising entropy term. In this paper, we set out to demonstrate that the further introduction of two additional latent losses to LeWorldModel, a backward dynamics predictor and an inverse dynamics action predictor, enforces further structure on the latent embedding, leading to further gains in both performance and planning efficiency. These are critical properties for improving the applicability of such methods to real-time model-based control of real-world robots. We demonstrate these gains on standard world model benchmarks and two simulated robot manipulation tasks.

papers.title_en: Towards Probabilistically Safe Reinforcement Learning: Theory and Deployment on Humanoid and Aerial Robots
papers.authors: Pol Mestres, Varun Gabbita, Jason H. K. Siu, Sergio A. Esteban, Hampus Serneke, Joel W. Burdick, Aaron D. Ames
papers.evidence: 在 humanoid 与飞行机器人上验证的安全强化学习理论
papers.tldr: 标准强化学习不保证策略满足安全约束，而现有可证明安全的方法约束类型受限且难以与PPO等主流算法结合。作者扩展鲁棒安全梯度流强化学习框架，支持更一般的轨迹约束并放松对无偏估计的要求，使其可直接接入PPO。理论分析与在 humanoid 及飞行机器人上的部署验证表明该方法兼顾安全性与实用性，为安全关键场景的机器人强化学习提供可行路径。
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables robots to acquire complex skills, but standard RL formulations do not guarantee that learned policies satisfy safety constraints, which limits their use in safety-critical settings. Existing safe RL methods with provable guarantees typically support only restricted classes of constraints and require unbiased estimators of the objective and constraint functions, which prevents their direct integration with state-of-the-art algorithms such as proximal policy optimization (PPO). In this paper, we extend the recently introduced robust safe gradient flow-based reinforcement learning (RSGF-RL) framework to overcome these limitations. Our formulation accommodates a general class of trajectory-level safety constraints, including chance constraints such as collision avoidance with a prescribed probability, and our analysis allows for biased value and gradient estimators. We show that, with high probability, the constraint violation throughout training is bounded by the estimator bias plus a term that vanishes as the number of rollouts grows, and decays to this level if the initial policy is unsafe. We also establish the convergence properties of the iterates to approximate KKT points of the original safe RL problem. Finally, we show that RSGF-RL implemented with PPO-style estimates enables zero-shot sim-to-real deployment of whole-body control policies on a Unitree G1 humanoid and collision-free waypoint navigation on a Crazyflie drone.

papers.title_en: JEPA Dots: Dual-Latent World Model for Language-Guided Robot Control
papers.authors: Xianhao Pan, Chi Li, Hanchao Li, Yunxin Liu, Jiankai Sun, Luhui Hu
papers.evidence: 面向语言引导机器人控制的JEPA式双隐世界模型
papers.tldr: 针对语言引导机器人控制中指令既要影响动作选择又不能改变固定动作下预测后果的耦合难题，本文提出JEPA Dots双隐世界模型，将视觉动力学与语言任务表征分离学习，用掩码注意力把世界预测限制在与指令无关的动力学历史与给定动作上，并由任务特征引导流匹配策略。在40个LIBERO任务的闭环评测中取得84.9%的平均成功率，验证了联合嵌入预测架构在具身世界建模与控制中的有效性。
papers.abstract_en: Predictive world models for language-guided robot control face a fundamental conditioning challenge: instructions should influence action selection without altering the predicted consequences of fixed actions under identical observations. To address this challenge, we introduce JEPA Dots (Dynamics-Oriented Task Separation), a compact dual-latent framework that jointly learns visual dynamics and language-guided control through separate dynamics and task representations. Language-conditioned task features guide a flow-matching policy, while masked attention restricts world prediction to instruction-independent dynamics history and supplied actions. In closed-loop evaluation on 40 trained LIBERO tasks, JEPA Dots achieves 84.9% overall success with approximately 39.1M parameters, compared with the published 78.7% of NanoVLA-S with 161.0M parameters under a different evaluation protocol. In the reference experiment, JEPA Dots also improves overall success from 76.0% for our task-ID-conditioned adaptation baseline to 84.9%, with LIBERO-Goal success increasing from 67.1% to 88.5%. Instruction-switching experiments further confirm that task representations and policy outputs respond to language changes, while dynamics representations and world predictions remain invariant under fixed observations and supplied actions.

papers.title_en: Efficient VLA Reinforcement Learning via Subchunk Rollouts in Latent World Models
papers.authors: Nan Tang, Han-Tao Zhang, Jing-Cheng Pang, Hao-Nan Wang, Hao-Xiang Ren, Yi-Fei Sheng, Jun-Yin Ye, Tian Xu, Fan-Ming Luo, Hao-Xin Lin, Yang Yu
papers.evidence: 基于潜在世界模型的模型强化学习提升VLA效率
papers.tldr: 模型强化学习可借助想象经验改进预训练VLA策略，但现有方法依赖大规模图像或视频生成世界模型，计算开销巨大。LS-MBPO改用轻量潜在世界模型，提出分层强制训练，将密集因果监督与自回归反馈结合以缓解递归预测误差，并解决与VLA视觉输入接口不兼容的问题。实验表明该方法在显著降低开销的同时有效提升策略性能，为机器人强化学习提供了更实用的世界模型范式。
papers.abstract_en: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) can improve pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) policies through imagined experiences. However, existing VLA-MBRL methods primarily rely on large-scale image or video generation world models, incurring large computational overhead. Latent world models offer a more efficient alternative but face two challenges: compounding errors during recursive prediction and incompatibility with VLAs' visual input interfaces. In this work, we propose LS-MBPO, a lightweight residual MBRL framework that leverages latent world models to improve upon pretrained VLAs. LS-MBPO introduces two key techniques: (1) Hierarchical Forcing, which combines dense causal supervision with autoregressive feedback to mitigate compounding prediction errors; and (2) Latent Subchunk Rollouts, which leverage action chunks from a frozen VLA policy and a latent residual policy for successive subchunk refinement, bridging the gap between latent imagination and VLA policy execution. We further introduce a Progress-Conditioned Branch-Start Curriculum that progressively shifts rollout starting points from later to earlier task stages, enabling effective policy learning from short imagined rollouts. Extensive experiments on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and a real-world ALOHA robot show that LS-MBPO achieves superior task performance and training efficiency compared to existing methods.

papers.title_en: JEPA-ICL: Progress-Aligned Latent Plans for In-Context Robotic Manipulation
papers.authors: Tingjun Dai, Jianxiang He, Mingfei Han, Qihao Yu, Longtao Jiang, Changlin Li, Minghao Jin, Zhihui Li, Xiaojun Chang
papers.evidence: 在JEPA特征空间做预测规划并结合示范学习操作策略
papers.tldr: 示范数据在具身形态、外观与执行速度上的差异，使机器人难以判断哪些示范内容与当前进度相关。作者提出JEPA-ICL框架，在JEPA特征空间中预测到达子任务完成的有序未来状态以形成规划，并用这些规划在示范中定位进度对齐的上下文来指导动作生成。规划与动作共享同一策略并相互更新，使预测式规划与示范学习耦合起来，提升了跨具身操作中的进度感知与泛化能力。
papers.abstract_en: Demonstrations show how a task can be completed, but differences in embodiment, appearance, and execution speed make it difficult to identify the guidance relevant to the robot's current progress. We introduce JEPA-ICL, a vision-language-action framework that couples predictive planning with demonstration learning. The policy learns to plan by predicting ordered future states in JEPA feature space up to subtask completion, capturing what remains to be accomplished. These plans guide action generation and locate relevant stages in demonstrations, whose JEPA-supervised content features provide progress-aligned context. Learning from this context, in turn, updates the shared policy that produces the plans and actions. This coupling connects anticipating the robot's own execution with reusing demonstrated experience. On the Imitator Game, JEPA-ICL achieves 80.0% seen-task success under C15 pretraining, outperforming Zero-WAM by 12.0 percentage points. Without contextual demonstrations, JEPA-ICL outperforms the VLA-JEPA variant without human-video pretraining, improving success rates from 96.1% to 97.6% on LIBERO and from 62.9% to 73.2% on LIBERO-Plus. With demonstration-based training and contextual guidance at inference, LIBERO-Plus success further increases from 73.2% to 75.2%.

papers.title_en: Continuous-Action World Models: Learning Cross-Embodiment Spatiotemporal Dynamics Priors
papers.authors: Liangyu Li, Qingwen Liu
papers.evidence: 具备结构化潜函数空间、支持机器人动作生成的世界模型
papers.tldr: 跨不同机器人本体和执行频率的机器人策略学习缺乏统一的动作动力学先验。作者提出连续动作世界模型CoAWM，构建共享的潜函数空间刻画机器人动作的时空结构，并通过函数预训练将不同本体、不同采样频率的轨迹映射到统一表征，以动作重建和时间采样一致性学习共享动力学先验。该框架扩大了可用于预训练的数据来源，为跨本体的动作生成与世界建模提供了可扩展的基础。
papers.abstract_en: We introduce Continuous-Action World Models (CoAWM), a framework for learning cross-embodiment spatiotemporal dynamics priors that support robot action generation across embodiments and execution frequencies. At its core is a shared latent function space that captures the spatial and temporal structure of robot actions. We learn this space through two stages. First, function pretraining brings trajectories from different embodiments and sampling frequencies into a common representation, learning shared dynamics priors through action reconstruction and consistency across temporal sampling views. By accommodating heterogeneous robot trajectories, this stage broadens the range of data sources available for pretraining and facilitates scaling to larger and more diverse datasets. Second, we connect the pretrained function space to a world-model backbone, enabling observations, language instructions, and the current robot state to condition the prediction of a latent action function. A single decoder takes any query time and returns the corresponding end-effector action. By separating shared dynamics priors from task-conditioned action selection and temporal sampling, our approach provides a unified foundation for transferring robot experience across embodiments and control frequencies.

papers.title_en: HandMimicX: Learning Human-Like Dexterous Manipulation via an Object-Centric Policy from Egocentric Videos
papers.authors: Zihan Gao, Yufei Liu, Yuhong Zhang, Zhen Yu, Xinhao Huang, Zhinan You, Kai W. Ho, Zipeng Ye, Peng Jiao, Haoqian Wang
papers.evidence: 以物体运动为强化学习目标的物体中心策略学习
papers.tldr: 从人类视频学习灵巧操作难以把单次演示泛化到新空间位置并保持物理合理的手物交互。作者提出以物体为中心的框架，将强化学习目标定义为物体运动以解耦具体手部轨迹，并加入手物交互状态约束以获得更自然的手型。实验表明该策略可从自我中心RGB-D视频中学到空间可泛化且类人的灵巧操作技能。
papers.abstract_en: Learning dexterous manipulation from human videos remains an open challenge, particularly in the context of transferring a single demonstration into a spatially generalizable robotic skill and maintaining physically plausible human-like interactions. Unlike prior works that emphasize hand-motion imitation, we introduce an object-centric framework for acquiring dexterous skills from egocentric human RGB-D videos. Within our framework, we formulate the reinforcement learning (RL) objective in terms of object motion to decouple the underlying skill from the specific hand trajectory and impose constraints on hand-object interaction states to promote more anatomically natural hand configurations. Extensive experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate that our method enables efficient learning from human videos and generalizable skill transfer across novel spatial configurations.

papers.title_en: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
papers.authors: Gaoyue Zhou, Yvonne Wu, Zichen Jeff Cui, Nicolas Ballas, Mido Assran, Lerrel Pinto, Yann LeCun
papers.evidence: 支持具身智能体规划的分层世界模型
papers.tldr: 基于世界模型的规划可提升具身智能体的泛化，但长程任务受累积误差和搜索复杂度困扰，现有分层方法多用刚性宏动作或潜在技能导致表示脆弱。本文提出ID-WM分层世界模型，将状态空间可达性与局部控制解耦。高层采样可行转移，低层作为逆动力学求解器将转移落地为精确动作。该框架提升了长程规划的效率与精度。
papers.abstract_en: Planning with world models enables test-time adaptation for embodied agents, offering superior generalization over direct policy learning. However, long-horizon tasks remain hindered by cumulative errors and search complexity. Existing hierarchical methods often use rigid macro-actions or latent skills, leading to brittle representations and limited fine-grained control. We introduce ID-WM (Implicit Dynamics World Models), a hierarchical world model that decouples state-space reachability from local control. Our framework utilizes a high-level model to sample feasible transitions across the state manifold and a low-level world model as an inverse dynamics solver to ground these transitions into precise actions. This allows the planner to identify reachable subgoals without being constrained by low-level execution details. By prioritizing local physical feasibility over global behavioral patterns, ID-WM synthesizes novel long-horizon plans from short segments, transcending the specific behavioral modes seen during training. We demonstrate its effectiveness across three navigation and manipulation suites, achieving a 38.5% improvement over state-of-the-art policy and diffusion-based planners. Crucially, by leveraging this hierarchical structure to mitigate compounding errors, our approach yields a 135% performance gain over single-level world model MPC, particularly in complex, unseen configurations for long-horizon tasks. Videos can be viewed at https://id-wm.github.io

papers.title_en: SCOUT: Planning under Occlusion via Object-Centric World Model Rollouts
papers.authors: Amir Hossain Raj, Xuesu Xiao
papers.evidence: 基于物体中心世界模型推演的遮挡下规划
papers.tldr: 机器人在杂乱环境中常需从部分视角规划，前景遮挡使目标与自由空间信息缺失，反应式策略易忽略隐藏约束而穷举搜索代价过高。本文提出SCOUT，利用物体中心场景表示重建隐藏几何并导出包含遮挡层级与可达走廊的关系规划状态，再由大模型提出结构化动作候选并用蒙特卡洛树搜索推演评估。该框架在遮挡场景下实现了高层推理与物理推演的结合，为结构化世界模型驱动的规划提供了范例。
papers.abstract_en: Robots manipulating in cluttered spaces must often plan from partial views where foreground objects occlude the target, surrounding geometry, and usable free space. Reactive policies often miss these hidden constraints, while exhaustive search becomes computationally prohibitive in dense clutter. We present SCOUT, an occlusion-aware planning framework that bridges high-level deliberation with grounded physical rollouts. SCOUT leverages an object-centric scene representation to reconstruct hidden geometry and derive a relational planning state capturing blocker hierarchies and accessibility corridors. To navigate the vast action space in clutter, an LLM proposes structured action candidates which are then rigorously evaluated via Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) using a learned action-conditioned world model. Evaluations on 'Reveal' and 'Placement' tasks show that SCOUT outperforms Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, embodied agents, and 3D world models, with significant gains in long-horizon tasks requiring reasoning over occluded geometry. We further validate the framework's robustness through real-world robotic manipulation in a cluttered shelf environment.

papers.title_en: PointPilot: Unified Robotic Manipulation via Object-Centric 3D Point Flow Prediction
papers.authors: Yihan Fang, Yuxin Tian, Ruixiang Wang, Zhanqi Zhang, Xing Hu, Zhen Yang, Huayi Zhou, Yongyi Su, Wei Gao, Kui Jia
papers.evidence: 以物体为中心的三维点流表示提升操作策略泛化
papers.tldr: 机器人操作策略的泛化性受具身、相机位姿与场景布局等多维域变化制约。PointPilot提出以任务为中心的物体级三维点流预测框架，只表示与任务相关的物体并把机械夹爪也视为物体，避免预测无关场景部分。它还将三维空间表示对齐到统一坐标系，支持闭环全自动动作执行。实验表明该物体中心表示在多种域变化下具备更强的操作泛化能力。
papers.abstract_en: Generalization remains a central challenge in robotics, calling for policies that address domain variations from multiple dimensions such as diverse embodiments, camera poses, and/or scene layouts. In order to approach this problem, we introduce PointPilot, a task-focused and 3D aligned manipulation framework built on a 3D space point-flow prediction. Rather than modeling the global scene, PointPilot only represents task-focused objects (robot grippers treated as objects), avoiding the prediction of potentially redundant scene parts unrelated to the manipulation tasks. Moreover, PointPilot aligns 3D spatial representation in one unified coordinate and supports closed-loop and fully automatic action execution across different manipulation modes from object point flow without a separately trained action expert, while existing works typically need an extra action head or are (semi-)automatic and single-arm mode specific. Given sensor observations and language instructions, our model jointly learns subtask planning, task-relevant object grounding, and 3D point flow prediction in an end-to-end way. By processing heterogeneous data in a shared 3D point flow space, PointPilot is able to absorb demonstrations from different embodiments. Extensive simulative and real world experiments validate our method. Notably, we demonstrate zero-shot embodiment generalization with PointPilot. A single trained policy can be deployed on previously unseen embodiments and successfully complete manipulation tasks without any additional fine-tuning.

papers.title_en: Learning Object-Centric Motion Priors from Human for Robotic Dexterous Manipulation
papers.authors: Zhengdong Hong, Guofeng Zhang
papers.evidence: 利用人-物交互数据学习物体中心运动先验用于灵巧操作
papers.tldr: 多指灵巧手操作多样物体时面临高维动作与复杂动力学挑战。作者利用人-物交互数据集，不只模仿人类示范，而是整体预测未来的手-物状态，并将预测的物体未来状态作为通用奖励项用于强化学习，从而减少任务特定奖励设计。在仿真与真实世界的三项操作任务上，该方法优于现有最优方法，提升了跨任务泛化能力。
papers.abstract_en: Manipulating diverse objects with multi-fingered dexterous hands is challenging due to the high dimensionality and complex dynamics. Human-Object Interaction (HOI) datasets provide rich knowledge about task information and embodied interactions. Instead of solely imitating the human demonstrations, our method learns to holistically predict future hand-object states by leveraging these datasets. The predicted future states of the object can serve as a general-purpose reward term for reinforcement learning, reducing reliance on task-specific reward engineering and enhancing generalization across tasks. We conduct extensive experiments on three manipulation tasks in simulation and the real world. Our approach outperforms existing SOTA methods in both success rate and generalizability on novel objects. Furthermore, we validate the cross-embodiment compatibility of our methods by successfully deploying the skills on different robot hands.

papers.title_en: SimDuoReal: Object-Centric Bimanual Policy for Emergent Dexterity
papers.authors: Qiyang Yan, Yulin Liu, Akash Sharma, Haozhi Qi, Guanya Shi, C. Karen Liu
papers.evidence: 面向双臂操作的对象中心强化学习策略与DAgger蒸馏
papers.tldr: 针对双臂灵巧操作中手臂与手部协调难以手工指定、奖励往往任务特定的问题，本文提出SimDuoReal，在共享的对象中心奖励下训练强化学习策略并变化训练环境，使预抓取、抓取重抓、手内调整与换手等行为自发涌现。随后在过渡状态上精修专家并用DAgger与强化学习蒸馏为单一策略，表明对象中心学习目标可有效驱动复杂双臂灵巧操作。
papers.abstract_en: Bimanual dexterous manipulation requires coordinated arm and hand control, yet specifying such coordination manually is challenging and often task-specific. In this work, we explore whether complex bimanual dexterity can emerge from a simple object-centric learning objective. We train reinforcement learning policies under a shared object-centric reward, varying their training environments rather than tuning separate rewards for each behavior. We find that the policies discover pre-grasp manipulation, grasping and regrasping, in-hand adjustment and handover to reach object-pose goals without hand-designed motion sequences. We then refine the experts on transition states and use DAgger and reinforcement learning to distill them into a single policy that composes these behaviors for diverse bimanual tasks. On real hardware, the same policy succeeds in 61 of 80 trials (76.3\%) across four tasks with unseen objects and no task-specific fine-tuning. In simulated barcode scanning, our policy achieves 85.0\% success, compared with 60.4\% for two single-arm policies without handover. These results suggest that this objective provides a simple and scalable interface for learning general bimanual dexterity, shifting the burden from manually designing robot coordination to specifying what should happen to the object.

papers.title_en: Decoupled Asynchronous System for Humanoids (DASH): Latency-Agnostic Scaling of Vision-Language-Action Models for Humanoid Manipulation
papers.authors: Bingzhang Wang, Nathan Zhao, Jialeng Ni, Jiayin Zheng, Yin Zhang, Kehua Chen, Jian Yao
papers.evidence: 面向人形灵巧操作的异步视觉语言动作系统
papers.tldr: 视觉语言动作模型在闭环控制中因骨干网络位于控制关键路径上，导致执行动作基于过时观测，限制人形灵巧操作的响应性。本文提出DASH，将策略解耦为慢速视觉语言模型与快速流匹配动作头，通过LCM通信协议并发运行，使控制频率由快速动作头决定。该设计在保持大模型能力的同时提升了人形操作的实时性与稳定性，为面向人形机器人的全身操作控制提供了系统级方案。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) models pair a vision-language backbone with an action head, but in closed-loop control the backbone sits on the control-critical path: while it computes, the robot keeps moving, so each executed action is conditioned on an increasingly stale observation. A larger backbone therefore directly blocks reactivity, especially in humanoid dexterous manipulation. We present DASH, a Decoupled Asynchronous System for Humanoids that removes this coupling. DASH splits the policy into a slow vision-language model (System 2) and a fast flow-matching action head (System 1) that run as concurrent processes over the LCM communication protocol, so the control rate is set by the action head alone, independent of backbone size. The action head fuses stale semantics from a frozen backbone with fresh vision from its own ResNet encoder, desynchronized training exposes it to the staleness it meets at deployment, and an adaptive temporal aggregator aligns overlapping action chunks under variable inference latency. On an asynchronous RoboTwin benchmark that charges inference latency in simulated time, DASH holds 20 Hz control rate from 0.8B to 8B backbones while the synchronous rate falls from 9.7 to 4.1 Hz, with higher success at every size. On a real humanoid with dexterous hands, DASH achieves clearly higher pick-and-place success than the synchronous pipeline.

papers.title_en: Ego Guidance: Enhancing Robot Policy Learning with Action-Free Human Egocentric Videos
papers.authors: Lin Long, Tianren Ma, Zhong Chu, Di Wu, Maosong Cao, Qixiang Ye, Junbo Zhao, Shanghang Zhang
papers.evidence: 利用第一视角视频进行机器人策略表示学习
papers.tldr: 如何利用无动作标注的人类第一视角视频提升机器人策略学习仍具挑战。本文提出SPAR，在混合Transformer架构中将未来视觉状态预测与动作预测结合，使表示学习获得独立互补的监督信号。实验发现由第一视角视频学到的表示能提升机器人在分布外任务上的表现，并随视频数据规模增长而进一步获益，为可扩展的机器人表示学习提供了思路。
papers.abstract_en: In this paper, we investigate how human egocentric videos can benefit robot policy learning without action supervision. Building on a pretrained VLM, we propose Shared Prediction on Action and Representation (SPAR), an MoT architecture in which future visual state prediction can provide independent and complementary learning signals alongside action prediction. We find that representations learned from egocentric videos improve downstream performance on out-of-distribution robot tasks, with further gains as video data scales. We also study the effects of objective choices and data curation, providing insights into how to leverage action-free videos for scalable robot learning.

papers.title_en: CIALLO: Learning Shared Intent Representations for Cross-Embodiment Manipulation
papers.authors: Choo Sin Wai, Dake Zhong, Jingye Zhang, Zhifang Liu, Siyao Xiao, Zirong Ding, Yuhong Zhang, Kangjie Chen, Dongbin Zhang, Guorui Song, Guocun Wang, Peng Jiao, Haoqian Wang
papers.evidence: 面向跨本体操作的共享意图表征学习
papers.tldr: 跨本体迁移操作知识需要能弥合不同控制接口的表征，而仅做动作重建不足以保证行为共享。CIALLO提出动作编解码器，将动作、视觉变化与观测接地语言对齐到短时程行为意图共享空间，并由本体条件解码器映射回具体机器人动作。在八种本体上预训练后，仅需一段不超过10秒的示教即可适配新机器人。
papers.abstract_en: Robot demonstrations contain reusable manipulation knowledge, but transferring this knowledge across embodiments requires representations that bridge differences in control interfaces. Action reconstruction alone does not ensure that similar behaviors across robots share a representation. To address this gap, we introduce CIALLO, an action codec that aligns actions, visual changes, and observation-grounded language in a shared space of short-horizon behavioral intent. An embodiment-conditioned decoder maps this intent back to robot-specific actions, allowing a shared representation to support different control interfaces. After pretraining on eight embodiments, CIALLO adapts to a new robot from one recording of at most 10 seconds by updating only its embodiment embeddings. The calibrated codec then remains frozen while a policy learns to predict intent from observations and instructions. We instantiate this policy with Qwen3.5-4B to form Qwen-CIALLO, whose backbone requires no large-scale robot-action pretraining before policy finetuning. With 20 demonstrations per task, Qwen-CIALLO achieves 76.7\% average success across real SO-101 and single-arm Piper robots, compared with 70.0\% for fully finetuned $\pi_0$. In simulation, we additionally finetune the action decoder, achieving 97.3\% success on LIBERO and 52.7\% on RoboTwin 2.0. The LIBERO policy also achieves 80.8\% on LIBERO-Plus without further finetuning. Together, these results support a shared action codec as a transferable control interface that separates embodiment calibration from task learning.

papers.title_en: Body Schema Policy: Body as the Vision-Action Interface for Efficient Robot Loco-Manipulation
papers.authors: Lechen Zhang, Chenyuan Chen, Muxin Zhou, Zewen He, Yoshihiko Nakamura
papers.evidence: 用于视觉-动作控制的潜在身体图式结构化表示
papers.tldr: 现有机器人全身移动操作依赖超大模型规模且需任务微调，效率低下。本文提出Body Schema Policy，将身体图式作为视觉-动作接口，把关节与连杆令牌置于运动学树上，用螺旋运动传递特征。通过身体查询视觉，每个部位检索自身视觉证据以条件化动作去噪。该方法以结构化表示实现了高效的移动操作策略学习。
papers.abstract_en: Currently, robots can learn whole-body loco-manipulation through scale: the strongest policies have billions of parameters and still need task-specific fine-tuning. Humans have limited processing capacity, yet learn and act efficiently through a body schema that organizes what they see and how they move. We introduce Body Schema Policy (BSP), an imitation learning policy that builds such a schema into the vision-action interface. Its latent body schema places joint and link tokens on the robot's kinematic tree, where learned screw motions carry features between links. Through body-queried vision, each body part retrieves its own visual evidence, which conditions the denoising of its actions. With this inductive bias, BSP returns an action chunk faster than any policy we compare. Compact, body-specific visual readouts also emerge without spatial supervision: manipulation commands depend strongly on task objects, while locomotion commands respond more broadly to the scene. On nine simulated Unitree G1 whole-body tasks, BSP matches the $Ψ_0$ humanoid foundation model with $75\times$ fewer parameters and nearly doubles Diffusion Policy's success. The same holds on a real G1 and a Fetch mobile manipulator.

papers.title_en: SemPhys: Semantic-Physical Co-Learning for Humanoid Motion Generation via Differentiable World Models
papers.authors: Zejian Kang, Yeqiang Wang, Zekai Chen, Boyang Shen, Mingyu Ma, Bingqian Wu, Fan Zhou, Jianjie Zhang, Chentao Shen, Wentao Yang, Rui Qian, Xiangru Huang
papers.evidence: 用可微世界模型与语义反馈生成人形全身运动
papers.tldr: 语言指令驱动机器人全身运动时，跟踪控制器在接触约束下维持平衡会使执行动作偏离参考并改变语义。作者提出SemPhys，用可微世界模型在仿真执行上提供语义反馈来训练运动生成器，直接在物理执行完整动作上评估语义对齐。该方法缓解了参考与执行语义不一致问题，为人形机器人全身控制与交互提供新范式。
papers.abstract_en: In human-robot collaboration, natural language lets people direct a humanoid's whole-body movements without programming joint trajectories. A common approach generates a kinematic reference from an instruction and relies on a tracking controller to execute it. However, as the controller maintains balance under contact constraints, the executed motion can depart from the reference in ways that change the action it conveys. Our central insight is that semantic alignment must be evaluated directly on the complete motion the robot physically executes. Building on this insight, we introduce \textbf{SemPhys}, a framework that trains motion generators using semantic feedback from simulated executions. A differentiable world model and a fixed tracking controller predict a short segment of a recorded execution. SemPhys inserts this prediction at its original position, scores the complete trajectory against the instruction, and backpropagates through the predicted segment. A paired anchoring loss stabilizes adaptation by keeping each generated reference close to its counterpart from the initial generator. On BONES-SEED, SemPhys largely preserves instruction retrieval accuracy from reference to execution and achieves the highest retrieval accuracy on executed motions among the evaluated methods.

papers.title_en: Embodied Graph: A Relational World Model for Long-Horizon Tasks
papers.authors: Zongyuan Wu, Xin Wang, Tongtong Feng, Yuan Meng, Zeyang Zhang, Ling Feng, Wenwu Zhu
papers.evidence: 基于稀疏状态抽象的关系世界模型用于规划
papers.tldr: 现有世界模型依赖稠密像素观测，易吸收冗余信息并忽略实体关系，导致长程想象滚动中误差累积。本文提出在稀疏状态抽象上进行想象的关系世界模型，构建紧凑状态并建模任务相关实体间的关系。方法通过去除冗余与关系建模提升长程规划稳定性。该工作为长程具身任务提供了更鲁棒的世界模型框架。
papers.abstract_en: Long-horizon tasks in embodied and web environments involve extended decision sequences and delayed feedback, making accurate planning crucial for success. World models tackle this by learning latent dynamics for imagination-based planning. However, existing approaches merely rely on dense pixel-level observations, which forces the model to absorb redundant information while overlooking relations among task-relevant entities. Consequently, small errors may accumulate over long imagined rollouts and gradually corrupt the predictions. In this paper, we explore world models that imagine over sparse state abstractions, which poses two key challenges: 1) how to remove redundant information and form a compact state abstraction; 2) how to incorporate the relational structure to learn reliable long-horizon dynamics. To address these challenges, we propose Embodied Graph, a relational state abstraction that supports structured dynamics modeling and long-horizon imagination, and the Relational World Model (RWM), which performs imagination directly over graph states. RWM consists of (i) a Task-Aware Embodied Graph Constructor that filters redundant details and maintains graph memory through online updates, and (ii) an Embodied Graph Recurrent State Space Model that learns node-wise latent dynamics while capturing inter-node dependencies. The imagined graph states provide predictions of action consequences to guide decision-making. Experiments on Minecraft and Crafter demonstrate the effectiveness of RWM in embodied environments. Notably, in Minecraft, RWM is the only method that obtains diamonds within the given budget. Experiments on web interaction further illustrate the applicability of relational state prediction to the decision making process of web agents.

papers.title_en: Phoenix: Learning Scene Structure Representations for Generalizable World-Action Models
papers.authors: Yupeng Zheng, Chaoyue Li, Linbo Wang, Xiang Li, Yuhang Zheng, Xiaotong Su, Songen Gu, Yichen Zhang, Zebin Xing, Shuai Tian, Jingxiang Guo, Jing Li, Zhiyong Zhao, Zhongpu Xia, Qichao Zhang, Haoran Li, Shuicheng Yan, Dongbin Zhao
papers.evidence: 为世界-动作模型学习结构化场景表征并联合预测潜变量与动作
papers.tldr: 世界-动作模型联合预测未来观测与动作，但面向重建的视觉表征并未显式强调操作所需的空间关系与物体状态变化。作者提出Phoenix，通过双教师蒸馏将几何与时空语义知识注入DINOv3编码器，并用CS-VAE将特征因果聚合成保留场景布局的生成潜变量，最终联合预测潜变量与机器人动作。该结构化场景表征提升了世界-动作模型在操作任务上的泛化能力。
papers.abstract_en: World-action models jointly predict future observations and actions, yet reconstruction-oriented visual representations do not explicitly emphasize the spatial relationships and object-state changes needed for manipulation. We introduce Phoenix, which learns representations of scene structure for world-action modeling. Specifically, Phoenix Encoder enriches DINOv3's general visual semantics through dual-teacher distillation of geometric and spatiotemporal semantic knowledge. Next, CS-VAE causally aggregates and compresses Phoenix Encoder features into generative latents while preserving scene information and spatial layout. Finally, Phoenix jointly predicts these latents, complementary appearance latents, and robot actions, linking scene evolution with action generation. To study pretraining data efficiency, we curate approximately 39,000 hours of egocentric and robot manipulation data for representation learning and use the robot demonstration subset for WAM pretraining. Following benchmark-specific post-training, Phoenix achieves state-of-the-art performance across simulation and real-robot benchmarks spanning single-arm, bimanual, and dexterous manipulation. It demonstrates strong robustness to perturbations, achieving success rates of 94.8% on LIBERO-Plus and 72.4% on RoboTwin 2.0 C2R, alongside strong cross-embodiment transfer and real-world manipulation performance on Bench2Dex and RoboDojo-RealWorld, respectively. Pretraining-scale analysis shows larger performance gains from data scaling than a video-VAE-only baseline, indicating stronger scaling benefits and more effective data utilization. Moreover, Phoenix maintains high success rates when adapted with limited downstream demonstrations, demonstrating strong few-shot adaptation. Our code, pretraining data, and models are available on the project page to help the community reproduce our results.

papers.title_en: ECHO: In-Context Behavior foundation model for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
papers.authors: Xingyi Wang, Bin Li, Jiyuan Shi, Chenyun Zhang, Weiji Xie, Xiangyu Miao, Junsong Wu, Wei Song, Shiqiang Zhu, Chenjia Bai
papers.evidence: 面向人形全身强化学习控制的上下文行为基础模型
papers.tldr: 人形行为基础模型虽经大规模运动模仿与并行强化学习获得多样技能，但难以在不同物理条件下精确执行。本文提出ECHO上下文行为基础模型，将通用行为能力和动力学特定执行分离。方法采用混合退火采样建立行为先验，并通过上下文表示实现环境自适应控制。该工作提升了人形全身控制在多变物理条件下的精度。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid behavior foundation models (BFMs) acquire diverse skills through large-scale motion imitation and massively parallel reinforcement learning, yet broad behavioral capability does not ensure precise execution across physical conditions. Without distinguishing the underlying dynamics, policies may favor conservative compromises over environment-specific precision. We introduce ECHO, an in-context BFM that turns interaction experience into environment-specific control, separating general behavioral capability from dynamics-specific execution. Mixed and Annealed Sampling first establishes a behavior prior in a single pretraining stage by balancing targeted practice with broad motion coverage. Building on this prior, Context Representation and Residual Adaptation learns structured dynamics representations from interaction histories to guide residual corrections to the frozen prior, enabling adaptation without test-time parameter updates. Extensive experiments show that ECHO outperforms all baseline methods across diverse motions and physical conditions. Moreover, deployment on the Unitree G1 demonstrates whole-body teleoperation spanning extreme acrobatics and terrain interaction, alongside payload adaptation in manipulation and whole-body control. Page is available at https://mwondering.github.io/echo-bfm/

papers.title_en: Where Structure Enters a World Model: From Predictive Fit to Physical Rollout
papers.authors: Panayiotis Christou, Satyapragnya Kar, Flavjo Xhelollari, Parijat Dube, Rajarshi Das
papers.evidence: 研究物理结构如何增强包括JEPA式在内的预测世界模型
papers.tldr: 预测式世界模型虽能短期拟合观测，却未必产生长期物理一致的行为。作者系统研究物理结构进入世界模型的多种方式，在行星运动令牌模型与机械系统JEPA式视觉模型中考察守恒量监督、对称感知表示、时序一致性与结构化动力学。实验表明角动量监督可改善自主预测，而时序正则收益依赖配套物理目标与表示，为结构化世界模型设计提供了经验指导。
papers.abstract_en: Predictive world models learn to forecast observations, but accurate short-term predictions do not necessarily produce physically coherent behavior over longer horizons. We investigate how incorporating physical structure can strengthen world models while retaining their underlying predictive objectives. Across token-based models of planetary motion and JEPA-style visual models of mechanical systems, we study conserved-quantity supervision, symmetry-aware representations, temporal consistency, and learned structured dynamics. In planetary motion, angular-momentum supervision improves autonomous next-token forecasting, while the benefits of temporal regularization depend on the accompanying physical objective and representation. In visual models, generating rollouts through supervised energy-based dynamics heads produces more faithful trajectories and phase-space evolution. Together, these findings highlight the importance of how physical structure participates in prediction: improvements in an auxiliary physical readout or a local acceleration estimate do not automatically translate into more reliable long-horizon behavior. Evaluations across initial conditions and physical parameter shifts further reveal where these benefits persist and where generalization remains limited. Our study supports physical structure as a practical means of improving predictive world models and provides a unified framework for understanding its effects on representations, learned transitions, and autonomous rollouts. The central lesson is that effective physical inductive biases should help models both represent physical regularities and use them to generate future states.

papers.title_en: CHAMP: Coordinated Humanoid Loco-Manipulation with Whole-Body Motion Priors
papers.authors: Lijun Han, Muyuan Ma, Zichen Wang, Siyuan Liu, Yuxi Liu, Yutong Wang, Bohao Zhang, Heng Zhou, Wei Sui
papers.evidence: 基于共享运动先验的人形全身移动操作与物体交互
papers.tldr: 协调移动与灵巧操作是人形机器人在人类环境中作业的核心能力，难点在于从多样数据中学习运动先验并有效用于全身控制。作者提出CHAMP，用约2298小时异构人体与机器人数据预训练视觉语言模型以预测未来身体与手部运动，并通过共享运动表示实现跨具身的统一全身运动学习。为将先验落地到控制，引入协调机制把运动先验接地为机器人全身控制策略，实现了人形移动操作的一体化。
papers.abstract_en: Coordinating locomotion and dexterous manipulation is fundamental to humanoid robots operating in human environments. A key challenge is learning motion priors from diverse data and using them effectively for coordinated robot control. We present CHAMP, a unified framework for humanoid loco-manipulation that combines whole-body motion pretraining with adaptive feature extraction. CHAMP pretrains a vision-language model to predict future body and hand motion from approximately 2,298 hours of heterogeneous human and robot data. A shared motion representation enables unified whole-body motion learning across embodiments from datasets with body annotations, hand annotations, or both. To ground these motion priors in robot control, we introduce a Coordination-oriented Action Expert (CAE) and train it on replay data generated using the target controller. Through sparse routing, CAE adaptively selects, transforms, and fuses features from multiple layers of the pretrained model to jointly generate body and hand actions. In experiments, CHAMP achieves overall success rates of 84.8% on seven simulated tasks and 91.4% on seven real-world tasks with a Unitree G1, outperforming the evaluated baselines in both settings. In particular, CHAMP achieves 70.0% success on the long-horizon popcorn-serving task, compared with 40.0% for the best-performing baseline.

papers.title_en: ActField: Learning Action Effects as Continuous-Time Latent Dynamics
papers.authors: Yunpeng Qing, Yuheng Huang, Changxu Wei, Yilun Kong, Yichen Shi, Shunyu Liu, Changqing Zou
papers.evidence: 将动作效果学习为潜动力学的连续时间JEPA世界模型
papers.tldr: 现有动作条件JEPA世界模型只在离散观测间隔预测未来表示，使动作效果的时序演化保持隐式。作者提出ActField，用作用在物理时间上积分的动作条件向量场显式建模潜状态演化，并将与动作无关的演化同动作诱导的变化分离，后者由潜上下文调制；参考条件表示与多步动力学损失进一步增强长时程预测。该工作给出了结构化且连续时间的具身世界建模方式，有助于预测与决策。
papers.abstract_en: Learning how actions change visual states is essential for prediction and decision-making in embodied tasks. Existing action-conditioned JEPA world models typically predict future representations at discrete observation intervals, leaving the temporal evolution of action effects implicit. We introduce ActField, a continuous-time JEPA world model that explicitly models latent state evolution through an action-conditioned vector field integrated over physical time. ActField separates action-independent evolution from action-induced changes, with the latter modulated by the latent context. A reference-conditioned representation and multi-step dynamics loss further support accurate long-horizon prediction. Together, these components provide a structured and temporally continuous formulation for predicting action-conditioned visual dynamics. Experiments across LIBERO, DROID, and BEHAVIOR demonstrate improved visual prediction fidelity and more accurate action-induced motion prediction over existing world models. Further evaluations on simulated and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate the utility of ActField in improving downstream policy planning through VLM-guided action selection.

papers.title_en: Foresight Forcing: Learning Spatial Foresight for Robotic Manipulation
papers.authors: Mishuo Han, Zhixuan Liang, Zhaoyuan Wan, Wendi Chen, Jiarui Chen, Xinkai Wang, Yue Ma, Yu Zhou, Junting Chen, Yao Mu, Jun Lv, Chuan Wen, Cewu Lu
papers.evidence: 为机器人操作策略学习空间转移表示
papers.tldr: 现有世界动作模型虽能预测未来视觉观测，但其训练目标未显式建模三维几何变化。本文提出Foresight Forcing，利用冻结的三维基础模型从当前与未来观测中提取稠密特征差作为监督，并将其蒸馏为空间转移查询。该方法提升了机器人操作策略对物体运动与空间关系变化的预判能力。这一表示学习思路为操作策略提供了几何感知的结构化先验。
papers.abstract_en: Robotic manipulation policies can improve action prediction by anticipating how objects move and how their spatial relationships change. World Action Models (WAMs) learn to predict future visual observations, but their training objectives typically leave the underlying 3D geometric transitions implicit. To alleviate this problem, we introduce Foresight Forcing ($\mathcal{F}^{2}$), a WAM that learns a spatial transition representation from changes in a pretrained 3D feature space. During training, a frozen 3D foundation model extracts patch-wise feature differences from aligned current and future observations that provide dense supervision for geometry-aware feature transitions. We distill these targets into spatial transition queries, which are progressively refined from the current observation, language instruction, and proprioceptive state, and use them alongside current visual features to generate actions. At deployment, the policy predicts the queries without future observations or the 3D teacher. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin2.0 demonstrate strong manipulation performance and improved robustness, including 95.01% average success on RoboTwin2.0 Full. On six real-world manipulation tasks, $\mathcal{F}^{2}$ achieves a mean task score of 85.8%.

papers.title_en: PreWAM: Exploring the Design of Latent Future Prediction for World-Action Modeling
papers.authors: Wan Chi, Sen Li, Zihang Cui, Chuqin Huang, Yunlong Wang, Nanshan Deng, Yanjun Huang
papers.evidence: 面向世界-动作模型的结构化潜在未来预测
papers.tldr: 世界-动作模型依赖未来预测作为策略学习的监督信号，但不同预测空间对泛化性的影响缺乏系统研究。作者通过受控实验发现，基于DINO特征的空间结构化语义特征在视觉扰动下泛化更好，运动信息也更易从预测表示中恢复。据此提出PreWAM，以残差世界预测在该空间中联合学习相对状态变化与未来状态，强调动态信息的同时保留未来监督。该设计为世界-动作模型的预测空间选择提供了可复用的经验依据。
papers.abstract_en: World-action models combine action generation with future prediction, allowing visual transitions to serve as supervision for policy learning. Our controlled study of prediction spaces shows that spatially structured semantic features support better overall generalization under visual perturbations and make motion information more readily recoverable from learned predictive representations. Building on these observations, we introduce PreWAM, a world-action model that organizes future supervision around state changes in a prediction space defined by pretrained DINO features. Specifically, Residual World Prediction jointly learns source-relative changes and their resulting future states to emphasize dynamic information while preserving future-state semantics. Temporal-Scale Prediction conditions world queries on temporal distance to capture both short-term local motion and longer-horizon state evolution. These predictive objectives jointly shape a shared vision-language backbone with action supervision during pretraining and downstream policy learning. Experiments across the LIBERO benchmark family, SimplerEnv, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world robotic manipulation demonstrate strong manipulation performance and improved generalization and robustness under diverse distribution shifts.

papers.title_en: EffectWAM: Learning Action-Grounded Effects for Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Yuan Zhang, Hao Cui, Jingfei Ni, Meiyi Wang, Xin Nie, Chi Liu, Wenjie Xu, Lin Gao, Hao Li, Xianhe Zhang, Jiajia Wu, Diyuan Liu, Jia Pan, Chao Ji
papers.evidence: 将视觉预测与可执行机器人控制结合的世界动作模型
papers.tldr: 世界动作模型需要把视觉预测与可执行控制真正连接起来，但现有表示往往缺少动作与几何约束。作者提出EffectWAM，用独立编码的未来观测与当前锚点之差表示视觉变化，引入相机位姿编码，并通过动作接地训练视觉表示保留末端位姿与夹爪状态变化。该方法使视觉预测更贴合可执行动作，为机器人操作中的世界动作建模提供了结构化设计。
papers.abstract_en: World-action models connect visual prediction with executable robot control. We present EffectWAM, which develops this connection through three complementary components: Effect, camera positional encoding (CaPE), and Action Grounding. Effect represents visual change as the difference between independently encoded future observations and a shared current-observation anchor. CaPE conditions endpoint pooling on relative camera pose when reliable extrinsics are available, while sharing the same learned parameters with pose-free pooling for uncalibrated trajectories. Action Grounding trains the visual representation to retain measured changes in end-effector pose and gripper state. An exponential moving average of the observation encoder supplies Effect targets. A shared generation expert learns to jointly predict Effect and an executable action chunk through flow matching, and reuses the sampled pair to generate future video on demand. This allows the controller to execute actions without waiting for video synthesis. We train on more than 20,000 hours of heterogeneous embodied data, excluding unused chain-of-thought data, and accommodate dataset-specific joint, end-effector, and hand-pose representations. Our evaluation uses the Small (8B) configuration on all five benchmarks and additionally evaluates the Large (26B) configuration on RoboDojo. Experiments examine closed-loop manipulation across complementary benchmarks, and comparisons across multiple baseline policies show consistent improvements from Action Grounding.

papers.title_en: DexWAC: A Unified World-Actor-Critic Model for Dexterous Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Hongjia Liu, Dacheng Zhou, Minghao Fu, Chuanjun Guo, Tianze Wang, Qingtao Liu, He Wang, Li Yi
papers.evidence: 统一的动作条件世界模型与演员-评论家
papers.tldr: 现有世界-动作模型只把未来观测预测当作辅助损失，而策略改进方法又分离学习动力学与价值，导致训练开销大、表征共享不足。本文提出DexWAC，在单一机器人预训练框架中联合学习动作器、动作条件世界模型与自举评论家，使灵巧操作策略同时获得预测与价值信号。实验表明统一建模在灵巧机器人操作任务上有效，为世界模型与强化学习融合提供了新范式。
papers.abstract_en: Robot demonstrations provide more than actions to imitate: they reveal how actions change the world and how those changes contribute to task success. Recent world-action models (WAMs) extend vision-language-action (VLA) models with the first signal by jointly predicting actions and future observations, yet this predictive ability serves only as an auxiliary loss for policy learning. Meanwhile, most policy improvement methods learn dynamics and values in separate models, increasing training overhead and limiting representation sharing between these complementary objectives. We introduce DexWAC, a unified world-actor-critic model that jointly learns an actor, an action-conditioned world model, and a bootstrapped critic in a single robot pretraining stage. Our key insight is that visual prediction encourages control-relevant features, while value supervision promotes task-relevant representations; together, they shape a representation suited to policy learning. Built on an image-editing backbone, DexWAC predicts, for each action chunk, the visual latent and proprioception at its endpoint together with its reward and continuation, so the world model alone efficiently yields complete imagined transitions without generating intermediate video frames. After adapting the world model and critic on real rollouts, we improve the pretrained actor through either PPO on imagined rollouts or critic-guided best-of-$N$ selection. DexWAC surpasses the large-scale pretrained VLA and WAM baselines in simulation and achieves 75% average success on two real-world tasks, compared with 45% for $π_{0.5}$. Its world model is more accurate and faster than video-based baselines, and ablations confirm that learning dynamics and value together improves the policy.

papers.title_en: Learning World Models through Contrastive Identification of Actions
papers.authors: Hayeong Lee, Youngjun Suh, Byung-Jun Lee
papers.evidence: 以对比式动作辨识学习潜在世界模型并支持目标导向规划
papers.tldr: 潜在世界模型可从离线视觉数据支持目标导向规划，但仅靠预测无法确定表示应保留哪些动作相关信息，而平方误差逆动力学监督信息有限。作者提出动作对比辨识CIA，在由历史条件化行为提议采样的候选中识别真实执行动作，从而奖励下一时刻潜在状态中超出历史的新信息。理论分析表明该方法可捕获逆回归误差无法反映的动作信息，实验显示其学习的世界模型表示更利于规划与控制。
papers.abstract_en: Latent world models enable goal-directed planning from offline visual data, but prediction alone does not specify which action-related distinctions their representations should preserve. Inverse dynamics provides auxiliary supervision, yet squared-error action regression rewards additional information only through changes in the conditional action mean. We propose Contrastive Identification of Actions (CIA), which identifies the executed action among alternatives sampled from a history-conditioned behavior proposal. Comparing actions plausible in the same context targets information supplied by the next latent beyond history. Under exact behavior matching, we show that CIA can reward action information that leaves optimal inverse-regression error unchanged, and verify this distinction through a controlled learning example. CIA achieves higher planner-averaged mean success than the base world model and a regression inverse-dynamics baseline across five visual control benchmarks, without modifying the planner.

papers.title_en: Dynamic Forcing: Learning Action-Grounded Sparse Dynamic Representations with Dense Future Guidance for World Action Models
papers.authors: Ziqiang Li, Shisheng Chen, Yunnan Wang, Wenyao Zhang, Zili Lin, Yuyang Zhang, Xudong Yang, Fangzhuo Jin, Chenyu Zhou, Wenjun Zeng, Xin Jin
papers.evidence: 世界动作模型中稠密未来引导的稀疏动态表示
papers.tldr: 世界动作模型通过视觉预测支持机器人控制，但稠密未来建模会重复编码当前观测中的静态上下文，而动作相关变化往往空间稀疏。本文提出CompactWAM，以当前观测为上下文锚点，用少量紧凑动态令牌表示预期变化，在视频监督的共享骨干中实现稀疏表示学习而无需重构目标。该框架在保持预测能力的同时提升了表示效率，为结构化世界模型辅助机器人控制提供了新思路。
papers.abstract_en: World action models (WAMs) support robot control through visual prediction, but dense future modeling repeatedly encodes static context already available in the current observation, while action-relevant changes are often spatially sparse. We study sparse dynamic representation learning, retaining the current observation as a contextual anchor and using a small set of compact dynamic tokens to represent anticipated changes. We develop CompactWAM, a sparse-dense joint predictive framework that enables sparse representation learning within a video-supervised shared backbone, without requiring a reconstruction objective for the sparse pathway. Since a limited token budget alone does not specify which information to retain, we introduce Dynamic Forcing, which pairs direct action supervision with privileged dense future guidance to promote action relevance and dynamic fidelity. While action prediction gradients directly drive compact tokens to capture control-relevant cues, dense future guidance further shapes them via action functional guidance that matches sparse and dense contributions to the action expert, and dynamics-aware distribution matching, which aligns temporal relational changes relative to a static reference. At inference, a single visual forward pass encodes current observations and compact dynamic tokens for action generation, eliminating dense future modeling. CompactWAM achieves 98.4\% success on LIBERO and 77.9\% on LIBERO-Plus, retaining respective success rates of 98.3\% and 76.6\% with only 9.2\% of the dense future token budget. Evaluations on RoboTwin~2.0 and real-world manipulation further demonstrate the effectiveness of the learned sparse predictive representations.

papers.title_en: FineDex: Bridging Fine-Grained Human-Object Interaction Generation to Dexterous Humanoid Manipulation
papers.authors: Yujia Zeng, Yuxin Chen, Yuzhen Song, Runhan Huang, Chensheng Peng, Yiyang Shao, Koushil Sreenath, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Yilun Du
papers.evidence: 以人-物交互先验驱动机器人灵巧人形操作
papers.tldr: 灵巧操作的核心是手指级控制，但现有人-物交互生成与灵巧操作方法难以指定交互如何执行，五指手常被简化为夹爪或直接复制人类演示。FineDex提出让手指级意图既可表达又可执行的框架，学习遵循手部选择、单指与关节物体接触等细粒度指令的人体-手-物体协同运动，并把生成交互作为可操作先验驱动机器人智能体发现物理可行的操作。实验验证了从生成到执行的有效桥接。
papers.abstract_en: Dexterity is, at its core, finger-level control, yet existing dexterous manipulation and human-object interaction (HOI) generation methods rarely let one specify how an interaction is performed: five-fingered hands are often reduced to grippers, or finger usage is copied from individual human demonstrations. We present FineDex, a framework that makes finger-level intent both expressible and executable. FineDex learns coordinated human body, hand, and object motions that follow fine-grained instructions on hand selection, individual fingers, and contacts with articulated objects. To bridge generation and execution, FineDex leverages generated interactions as actionable priors for an agent that discovers physically feasible contact strategies through practice in a physics-based digital twin. By adapting at test time without per-instance retraining, FineDex generalizes across fine-grained instructions and object configurations. Experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art HOI generation quality and fine-grained controllability, substantial improvements in dexterous manipulation success, and successful deployment on a real dexterous humanoid robot.
